reason: Combine rocky pebbles with shattered grains to advance the solid material toward forming worlds.
expectation: They may gather into larger rocky material, though the next stage is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The shattered grains might also gather with disk dust, but the rocky pebbles seem more directly relevant to the world-building goals.

effect: The pebbles and fragments formed a population of rocky bodies through concentration and gravitational collapse, providing material for the next stage.
reaction: The distinction between collapse and simple sticking was interesting.
reason: Slowly approaching bodies seem likely to merge and help build a larger world.
expectation: I expect some rocky bodies to gather into a larger body, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Fast projectiles could lead toward a collision, but building a larger body first seems useful.

effect: Slow accretion produced the young rocky world followed toward a hot interior and moon-forming impact.
reaction: The connection to the moon goal is clear.
reason: The crossing large worlds suggest an impact involving the young world, advancing the moon goal.
expectation: I expect a major collision that changes the young world, perhaps producing moon-forming debris.

alternatives.reason: Fast projectiles might break a smaller body, but I chose to follow the young world's path first.

effect: The impact melted the surviving world's interior; its moon has not yet formed.
reaction: It was useful to see that the original world survived the impact.
reason: Continue following the molten world toward the moon goal using the available fragments.
expectation: The fragments may change the world's composition or help produce debris; their role is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Fast projectiles may break a smaller body, but I want to follow the surviving world first.

effect: The added metal settled within the molten world, forming a dense core; the moon still remains to be made.
reaction: The differentiation into a core and lighter rock was a clear consequence of the molten interior.
reason: Another large impact may produce the debris needed for a moon.
expectation: I expect a collision that ejects material around the world, though it may take another step to form a moon.

alternatives.reason: Fast projectiles could advance the shattered-body goal, but I want to finish following the rocky world first.

effect: The grazing impact left the surviving world surrounded by orbiting debris, setting up moon formation.
reaction: The debris coming from both impact bodies makes the outcome feel connected to the collision.
reason: Combine the orbiting rubble with the debris cloud to advance the moon goal.
expectation: I expect the orbiting material to gather into a moon, though it may need another stage.

alternatives.reason: The fast projectiles could advance the shattered-body goal, but the moon seems close to completion.

effect: The orbiting debris gathered into a moon, completing the first goal; the shattered-body goal remains.
reaction: It was satisfying that the moon formed around the same world followed through the impacts.
reason: The only offered combination may break a rocky body and advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the fast projectiles to shatter a rocky body into fragments, though further steps may be needed to gather them.

effect: The projectiles shattered a smaller body, producing fragments available to gather into a new body.
reaction: The distinction between this smaller body and the surviving world is clear.
reason: The only offered combination brings the fragments together with slowly approaching bodies, advancing the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect some fragments to gather into a small rubble body, though another step may be needed.

effect: The fragments gathered into a distinct rubble world, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast between a loose rubble world and the moon-bearing world was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the same rocky world through a grazing impact to a moon was most worthwhile; the debris and survivor felt connected to the earlier choices.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding metal-rich fragments felt less engaging because their purpose was uncertain until the result explained core formation.

surprise.text: The initial pebbles and fragments formed rocky bodies through concentration and gravitational collapse, rather than simple sticking.

arbitrary.text: The metal-rich fragments' role was not clear to me before combining them with the molten world, although the resulting differentiation made sense.

continue.text: Yes; I would be interested in following how the distinct moon-bearing and rubble worlds develop, though the offered compatible combinations made the choices fairly guided.
